name: blast-charge-loading-ui
description: Visual verification of charge loading UI: per-hole charges, explosive types, amounts, charge-all, visual indicators. #554: charging a hole now queues a charge_hole PendingAction (a blaster loads one hole at a time, on foot) instead of writing chargesByHole instantly — every commit click here is followed by a wait_until step proving the count only advances once the order actually lands, with a mid-loading screenshot proving the ordered-but-unloaded ghost/ORDERED overlay is visually distinct from a landed charge.

steps.description: Staffed opening (#551): a driller with blasting + drill_rig licence, a blaster with a bare blasting licence (no vehicle — #554's charge_hole actions are on-foot, requiredVehicleRole: null), plus an unmanned drill_rig, are hired/purchased for free at game-open.

steps.command: drill_plan grid rows:3 cols:3 spacing:2 depth:6 start:15,15 diameter:0.089
steps.description: One decrement click on the spacing stepper (data-field="spacing") lowers it 3->2m (DEFAULT_SPACING_M, Drill.ts) before dragging, so the (15,15)-(19,19) rectangle computes the declared 3x3. #553: confirming the grid queues 9 drill_hole PendingActions and pushes 9 PlannedHoles into plannedDrillHoles — none are drilled yet, so holeCount stays 0 right after confirm. Spacing tightened from the original 5m (which needed 2 increment clicks) to 2m (needing 1 decrement) specifically to keep this 9-hole grid's total door-to-door drilling time inside the site's own bankruptcy-grace window (no income anywhere in this file) — sandbox-measured: 9 holes at spacing 5 land around tick 191 with cash already negative, at spacing 2 they land around tick 130 with over $12,000 still in hand. #947 CI-fix follow-up: `diameter:0.089` added to match Drill.ts's own DEFAULT_DIAMETER_M — the grid tool's interaction array below never clicks a diameter stepper, so it always confirms at the UI's 89mm default, not this command's own pre-existing 0.15 fallback (drillPlan.ts). That gap fed computeDrillHoleDurationTicks (DrillPlan.ts) a different diameter per mode, so command mode drilled ~1.7x slower than the real UI — the driller stayed busy on later holes for longer in command mode, dispatching to charge_hole later and never racing the blaster onto simultaneous completions, while interaction mode's faster drilling freed the driller (also blasting-qualified, staffed:true) early enough to land two charge_hole completions on the same tick and skip clean past the wait_until below's exact chargedCount:6 checkpoint (CI: 'stalled at 9 after 9000 tick(s)', never landing on exactly 6). Root cause confirmed by direct comparison of full step-09 state dumps between command and interaction mode (cash/minFatigue/pendingActionCount all diverged despite identical tickCount) and by replaying the identical command sequence directly in-browser (bypassing the panel's clicks) once with the declared 0.15 default (reached exactly 6) and once with 0.089 (skipped it) — unrelated to #947's vehicle driver-gating fix itself, which this scenario's drilling/charging never exercises.

expect.note: 3 rows x 3 cols = 9 holes ordered (ghosts), none drilled yet (#553)

steps.description: #553: drain the ordered plan — the staffed driller/drill_rig lands all 9 holes well inside this pad (sandbox-measured landing at tick 130 for this tight spacing:2 pattern).

expect.note: All 9 holes have landed — none lost, none left ordered forever.

steps.description: Speed up the charge-loading waits below — real-clock auto-tick at 1x would take a long time to drain even a single blaster's queue.

Per-hole charging is a real control now (gap G3, ChargeHoleList.ts): the Charge step renders a "Per Hole" section, one row per hole keyed by data-hole, each with its own commit button at [data-hole="<id>"] [data-action="charge-hole"]. That button dispatches `charge hole:<id> explosive:<selected> amount:<amount>kg stemming:<stemming>m` from the panel's current product card / amount / stemming values (ChargeStep.chargeHole, Charge.ts) — the same three values Charge All reads, so the steppers have to be driven to the declared numbers first. 2 amount decrements (5 -> 3kg) reach this hole's declared 3kg; stemming is already at the 2.0m default and boomite is already the selected product, so neither needs a click. #554: the commit click only *orders* the charge (queues one charge_hole PendingAction and writes a PlannedCharge into state.plannedChargesByHole) — chargesByHole, and therefore chargedCount, does not move until a blaster physically walks to the hole and finishes loading it, so chargedCount must still read 0 immediately after this click.

expect.note: #554: ordering a charge no longer lands it instantly — chargedCount stays 0 until the blaster's charge_hole action actually completes

steps.description: 5 amount increments (3 -> 8kg) off what the H1 row left behind. 8kg is exactly boomite's maxChargeKg, so this is the largest charge the amount stepper will hand a boomite hole — one more click is a no-op, not an overshoot. Ordered while H1's own charge_hole action is still in flight (or already queued behind it) — a single blaster works one hole at a time, so this order and H1's sit side by side in plannedChargesByHole until each is claimed in turn.

expect.note: #554: still nothing landed — H1 and H2 are both ordered, neither loaded yet

steps.description: 3 amount decrements (8 -> 5kg) and 5 stemming decrements (2.0 -> 1.0m) — the first step in this file to move stemming off its default. Three holes (H1, H2, H3) are now ordered but not yet loaded at once — enough for the wait_until step right after this one to catch a genuinely mixed state (some landed, some still ghost) rather than draining a single order.

expect.note: #554: three orders queued (H1, H2, H3), none loaded yet — plannedChargesByHole holds all three

steps.description: #554/#590: the blaster claims the nearest of the three ordered holes and finishes loading it — the first entry moves from plannedChargesByHole into chargesByHole. Screenshot taken right here on purpose: exactly one hole shows the loaded charge visuals while the other two (still in plannedChargesByHole) render the lightweight ORDERED ghost marker (CHARGE_ORDERED_COLOR/CHARGE_ORDERED_OPACITY, BlastPlanOverlay.ts) — this is the shot that proves the two are visually distinct. maxTicks/timeoutMs widened to the implementer's own calibrated per-order wait budget (#554 landed). (#554 follow-up: NOT run at 8x speed unlike other orderedChargeCount/chargedCount waits elsewhere -- this step deliberately checkpoints a specific mid-load count for a screenshot; speed-8x would overshoot past it before the 200ms poll catches the exact value, and would defeat the one-at-a-time visual pacing this file exists to demonstrate. The already-generous timeoutMs budget (raised earlier for the #554 timeout-mismatch fix) covers real-time draining at normal 1x speed instead.)

expect.note: one of the three ordered charges has landed; the other two are still ordered-but-unloaded

steps.description: #554/#590: drain the remaining two ordered charges (H2, H3) one at a time — a single blaster never loads two holes simultaneously. Budget doubled off the implementer's single-order figure to cover two sequential loads. (#554 follow-up: NOT run at 8x speed unlike other orderedChargeCount/chargedCount waits elsewhere -- this step deliberately checkpoints a specific mid-load count for a screenshot; speed-8x would overshoot past it before the 200ms poll catches the exact value, and would defeat the one-at-a-time visual pacing this file exists to demonstrate. The already-generous timeoutMs budget (raised earlier for the #554 timeout-mismatch fix) covers real-time draining at normal 1x speed instead.)

expect.note: all three individually-ordered charges (H1, H2, H3) have now landed

#554: Charge All queues a charge_hole order for every hole — including H1/H2/H3, replacing their outstanding order — but chargesByHole is untouched until each one actually lands, so the count stays at 3 right after the click

steps.description: Charge All commits whatever the steppers currently show, and the H3 row above left them at 5kg/1.0m — so reaching this step's declared 5kg/2m needs 5 stemming increments (1.0 -> 2.0m) before the click. Without them the click would silently order every hole at 1.0m stemming while the command field claimed 2m: exactly the class of drift the amount/stemming asserts are here to fail loudly on. #554: this orders 9 fresh charge_hole actions (one per hole, cancelling/replacing H1/H2/H3's already-landed entries with a new pending order and queuing H4-H9 for the first time) — none of the 9 lands the instant the button is clicked.

#554/#590: the bulk Charge All order drains through the same one-at-a-time blaster pipeline. Screenshot taken at the halfway point (5 of 9 loaded) for a second, denser mixed-state shot: several fully loaded holes next to several still-ordered ghosts. Budget widened to cover up to 6 sequential loads at the implementer's own per-order figure. (#554 follow-up: NOT run at 8x speed unlike other orderedChargeCount/chargedCount waits elsewhere -- this step deliberately checkpoints a specific mid-load count for a screenshot; speed-8x would overshoot past it before the 200ms poll catches the exact value, and would defeat the one-at-a-time visual pacing this file exists to demonstrate. The already-generous timeoutMs budget (raised earlier for the #554 timeout-mismatch fix) covers real-time draining at normal 1x speed instead. #947 CI-fix follow-up: checkpoint moved from 6 to 5 — staffed:true's driller is also blasting-qualified and joins the blaster once drilling is done, so the Charge All drain lands two holes on the very same tick at this point in the sequence (deterministically confirmed: 3->4->5->7->9, tick 177 landing both the 6th and 7th charge together). 6 is never observed as a value chargedCount actually holds, so a wait_until pinned to it can only ever exhaust its budget waiting on a value the drain skips straight past. 5 sits on the same landing sequence.)

expect.note: 5 of 9 holes loaded from the Charge All order; the remaining 4 are still ordered-but-unloaded

steps.description: #554/#590: drain the rest of the Charge All order — every hole is now loaded. (#554 follow-up: NOT run at 8x speed unlike other orderedChargeCount/chargedCount waits elsewhere -- this step deliberately checkpoints a specific mid-load count for a screenshot; speed-8x would overshoot past it before the 200ms poll catches the exact value, and would defeat the one-at-a-time visual pacing this file exists to demonstrate. The already-generous timeoutMs budget (raised earlier for the #554 timeout-mismatch fix) covers real-time draining at normal 1x speed instead.)

expect.note: Charge All has now landed on every hole

steps.description: Restore normal speed before the remaining player-driven step.

A single hole re-ordered after Charge All has already fully landed, which is the whole point of the per-hole rows. The explicit [data-step="2"] click is required: Charge All completed the plan, so the still-armed autoAdvance had already moved the panel on to Sequence and the Per Hole rows were hidden. 2 amount increments (5 -> 7kg) and 5 stemming increments (2.0 -> 3.0m) then reach the declared values. #554: this queues a fresh charge_hole order for H5 — chargesByHole['H5'] keeps its old (5kg/2m) value until the new order lands, so chargedCount is unaffected by this click.

expect.note: count is unchanged — H5 was already loaded by Charge All; this step proves one row can re-order one hole without disturbing the other 8, and that the re-order doesn't land instantly either

steps.description: #554/#590: drain H5's re-order before the scenario ends, leaving the site in a fully-landed state rather than one hole still mid-load.
